translationRepairs: There was a singer named Song Ronghua whose voice was clear and beautiful; he excelled at these songs and was celebrated in his day.
There was a palace lady, Song Ronghua (ronghua being a consort rank), whose voice was clear and beautiful; she excelled at these songs and was celebrated in his day.
容華 is a consort rank; the singer was a woman; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
My heart is on Penglai—yet Confucius the sage has gone, and Kuaiji holds his grave mounds.
My heart is on Penglai—yet the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, the sages, have gone, and Kuaiji holds his grave mounds.
周孔 is the Duke of Zhou and Confucius; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Duke Wen of Zhou, Chang, held this sagely virtue; though the realm was divided into three parts, he held two of them.
Chang, the Western Earl of Zhou, held this sagely virtue; though the realm was divided into three parts, he held two of them.
周西伯昌: Chang, Western Earl (later King Wen), not a duke; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
What can dispel this sorrow? Only Duke Kang wine.
What can dispel this sorrow? Only Du Kang's wine.
杜康 is the legendary wine-maker Du Kang, not a duke; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
The world speaks of Boyang, yet knows nothing of Laozi; Chisong and Wang Qiao, too, are said to have attained the Way.
The world says Boyang (Laozi) never knew old age; Chisong and Wang Qiao, too, are said to have attained the Way.
殊不知老 means he did not know aging; 伯陽 is Laozi himself; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Bright, bright shines my imperial ancestor; with Xuanyuan and Yaoh he shares their glory.
Bright, bright shines my imperial ancestor; his radiance shines high in equal glory.
軒燿 means lofty radiance, not the names Xuanyuan and Yao; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
How great Master Ye's saying is—I slacken the strings and hold myself back.
How great is the saying of Ziye (Shi Kuang)—I slacken the strings and hold myself back.
子野 is the courtesy name of the music master Shi Kuang; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Why use Duke Du and weigh down our sages and worthies?
Why use the Earl of Du and weigh down our sages and worthies?
杜伯 is the Earl of Du; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Quietly doing what is taboo—punishment tracks the act; Jie at last killed Long Feng, and Tang was sent away at Mingtiao.
Quietly doing what is taboo—punishment tracks the act; Moxi had Long Feng killed, and Jie was banished at Mingtiao.
末喜 is Jie's consort Moxi; it was Jie, not Tang, who was banished at Mingtiao; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Ah, Guo Sheng—the refined man of antiquity; how wise Yan Zhao was—he truly won a minister.
Ah, Guo Sheng—the refined man of antiquity; how wise King Zhao of Yan was—he truly won a minister.
燕昭 is King Zhao of Yan; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Alas for Bo Yi—Confucius named him a sage.
Alas for Bo Yi and Shu Qi—Confucius named him a sage.
夷叔 is Bo Yi and Shu Qi (cf. 二子 in s0828); 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Emperor Shun danced with shield and axe until the Miao people bowed to Yu.
Emperor Shun danced with shield and axe until the Miao people submitted to him of the Gui clan.
媯 is Shun's clan name, not Yu; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
Under Emperor Xiaohe, Luoyang magistrate Wang Jun came from Guanghan in Yizhou; as a young man he entered service and mastered the Five Classics and their glosses.
Under Emperor Xiaohe, Luoyang magistrate Lord Wang (Wang Huan) came from Guanghan in Yizhou; as a young man he entered service and mastered the Five Classics and their glosses.
王君 means Lord Wang; the magistrate was Wang Huan 王渙; 從 rank means lower grade of the rank, not honorary
